source.title: Apply: Surveys and Statistics
source.text: Some sixth-grade students want to get more food choices in the cafeteria. They will conduct a survey of students who buy lunch in the cafeteria. What questions should they include in their survey? Explain your choices.

source.title: Apply: Presidential Terms
source.text: A presidential term in the United States is four years. In 1947, Congress passed an amendment to limit the president to two terms. The number of terms served by each president of the United States from 1789 to 2021 is shown in the bar graph. Given this information, what prediction can you make about the number of terms the next U.S. president will serve in office?

source.title: Apply: Making Moves
source.text: A group of friends are planning to make a movie. They research the running times of movies made. The data they collected are shown in the histogram. They have asked for your advice on how long their movie should run. What do you recommend? Explain your recommendation based on the data presented in the histogram.

source.title: Apply: Real Estate
source.text: Terrance is helping his grandmother sell her house. He uses a real estate website to look at the recent sale prices of similarly-sized houses in their area and collects the information in the table shown. What do you think would be a fair, but competitive selling price for Terrance’s grandmother’s house?

source.title: Apply: Average Monthly Temperatures
source.text: The box plots show the average monthly temperatures for the same month in Chicago, IL, and Honolulu, HI. How do the monthly temperatures between the two cities compare?

source.title: Apply: Professional Basketball
source.text: The two box plots show the salaries for 15 players on two different professional basketball teams. A basketball player hopes to be drafted by a professional basketball team. Should he hope to be drafted by Team A or Team B?

source.title: Apply: Real Estate
source.text: Terrance is helping his grandmother sell her house. He uses a real estate website to look at the recent sale prices of similarly-sized houses in their area and collects the information in the table shown. What do you think would be a fair, but competitive selling price for Terrance’s grandmother’s house?

source.title: Apply: Running a Marathon
source.text: Evelyn is training to run a marathon on the path shown. Evelyn expects that she will need at least 4 hours to finish the race but hopes to finish in less than 5 hours. How many miles should Evelyn try to run each hour to achieve her goal?

source.title: Apply: Honor Roll
source.text: Shanice wants to be on the honor roll for the next marking period. She determines that her mean test score needs to be a least 90 in both math and science to be on the honor roll. Her test scores in math and science so far this grading period are shown. How likely is it that Shanice will make the honor roll?

source.title: Apply: Water Parks
source.text: Andrew and his friends want to visit a waterpark, but Andrew must take his younger sister who is 8 years old and can only ride waterslides that are less than 100 feet high. Which waterpark should they visit? Include the heights of the slides at the two parks in your recommendation.

source.title: Apply: Middle School Fundraiser
source.text: Some sixth-grade students will make 50 bags of honey granola to sell at a fundraising event using the recipe shown. They will put 2 cups of granola in each bag and will sell each bag for $5.

source.title: Apply: Metro Train Versus Car Cost
source.text: Yelina’s mother is considering a monthly transit pass for $145. The walk from the station to work takes about 25 minutes. Her current commuting budget is shown. What do you recommend? Estimate a 4-week month using the weekly budget shown. Compare costs and explain how travel time affects your choice.

source.title: Apply: Which Brand to Buy?
source.text: Deon needs dishwasher detergent. Compare the two brands shown. Which brand should he buy? Use a ratio table to compare the cost for the same number of loads. Show your work and label the units.

source.title: Apply: Street Corn Recipe
source.text: Eduardo is going to make 30 ears of grilled Mexican street corn for a party using the recipe shown. He has all the ingredients except Cotija cheese. Eduardo tells a friend he will buy four 10-ounce packages of cheese that each contains 2 cups. How would you respond to Eduardo?

source.title: Apply: Babysitting Pay
source.text: Claire, Yuzuki, and Nakai compared their time babysitting and their earnings from the previous weekend. A new family is looking for a babysitter and is offering $10.75 per hour.

source.title: Apply: Making Concrete
source.text: Michael’s mother needs to secure four posts for her garden fence. She uses the concrete mix shown for the project. Each post requires 250 ounces of concrete mix.

source.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
source.text: For this math model, assume the bridge can support 35,924,000 pounds of cars. An average midsize car has a mass of about 1,524 kilograms. About how many cars does the model allow? Use 1 lb ≈ 0.454 kg.

source.title: Apply: Car Sales
source.text: A car dealership’s sales for one month are shown. The owner of the car dealership needs to order 50 cars from the factory. Based upon the sales shown, how many of each type of car do you recommend that the owner order?

source.title: Apply: Sleepy Animals
source.text: How do the sleep times of the different animals compare? Order the animals from those that sleep the most to the least. Which animals’ sleep times surprised you? Explain why.

source.title: Apply: The Food Drive
source.text: The organizers of a food drive set a new goal for a second food drive. They hope to collect 140% as many cans as they did for the last food drive in which they collected 145 cans. About how many cans can the organizers expect to collect? Explain your reasoning.

source.title: Apply: Book Fair
source.text: Students were asked which night of the book fair they planned to attend. The results of the survey are shown. Twenty percent of the students who planned to attend on Wednesday attended on Thursday instead. Twenty-five percent of the students who planned to attend on Thursday attended on Friday instead. Which day, Thursday or Friday, had a greater actual attendance? How many more students attended that day?

source.title: Apply: Puzzle Problem
source.text: The percentage of each type of puzzle in a toy store before a sale is shown. During the sale, the store sold all of the 300-piece and 500-piece puzzles. They sold 120 puzzles. How many of each type of puzzle did the store have before the sale?

source.title: Apply: A New Park
source.text: Claire, a city horticulturist, is developing a new park to replace an old city lot. The center of the park will feature a koi pond that will cover 1,245 square feet. Eighty-five percent of the remaining space will be covered with grass seed. A 50-pound bag of grass seed covers up to 7,500 square feet. Straw is also needed to cover the grass seed. One bale of straw will cover about 500 square feet. Choose a question to answer. Question 1: How many bags of grass seed should be used to seed the park? Question 2: How many bales of straw should be used to cover the grass seed?

source.title: Apply: Painting a Cabin
source.text: Choose a method. Solve independently, justify your answer, then check the goal.

source.title: Apply: Budgets
source.text: The parking lot shown is being repaved. Asphalt for the parking lot costs $3.95 per square foot, while the cost of labor is about $3 per square foot. The project manager also budgets for the use of equipment, including fuel and potential repairs. How much money would you recommend the project manager budget to complete the project?

source.title: Apply: Flooring
source.text: A garden designer wants to cover a gazebo floor with tiles. The gazebo is shaped like a decagon with equal sides. If floor tiles cost $2.89 per square foot, what budget do you recommend the designer have for the tiles?

source.title: Apply: Buying Popcorn
source.text: You go to movie theater with your family. Your family likes to buy popcorn to snack on during the movie. The theater sells three different-sized boxes of popcorn. Which size and how many boxes would you buy? Explain.

source.title: Apply: Cookie Houses
source.text: A cookie house building kit contains three different cookie house kits. Which cookie matches with which cookie house? Explain your reasoning.

source.title: Apply: Painting a Bedroom
source.text: Tahira is planning to paint the walls of her bedroom, which is in the shape of a rectangular prism. The bedroom has one window and two doors. The dimensions of the window and doors are shown in the table.

source.title: Apply: The Louvre Pyramid
source.text: Choose a method. Solve independently, justify your answer, then check the goal.

source.title: Apply: Snack Bags
source.text: Andrew has four types of nuts and a different quantity of each type. He wants to make 4 snack bags for each type of nut and will not mix the nuts in the snack bags. What will be the weight of the snack bags for each type of nut? Explain your reasoning.

source.title: Apply: Square Mirrors
source.text: The side lengths of two mirrors are shown. About how many times greater is the area of mirror A than the area of mirror B?

source.title: Apply: Biology
source.text: James is studying the growth rate of a specific type of bacteria. He places three cells in a Petri dish and records the number of bacteria every five hours. The table shows his results. Choose a question to answer. Question 1: What power represents the number of bacteria recorded every 5 hours? Question 2: What power would represent the number of bacteria after 25 hours?

source.title: Apply: Missing Parentheses?
source.text: Akela has been given a challenge by his math teacher to see how many different values the expression shown can have depending on where one set of parentheses is placed. How many different values can you come up with?

source.title: Apply: Acceptable Quality Levels
source.text: Some industries set three different levels of defects: critical, major, and minor. The AQLs for an automotive supplier are shown. If any of these defects exceed the acceptable percentage, the factory can pause further production to examine the source of the defects. A lot of 1,500 sensors had 0 critical defects, 25 major defects, and 143 minor defects.

source.title: Apply: Bonus Points
source.text: Anwar’s quiz bowl team must correctly answer the question shown to earn ten bonus points in their match. How should Anwar’s team respond if they want to earn the ten bonus points?

source.title: Apply: Party Plans
source.text: Reginald is having hot dogs at his party and 24 people are coming. His mom wants to have the same number of buns and hot dogs. Hot dogs and buns come in the packs shown. How many packs of each do you recommend that she buy? Explain your reasoning.

source.title: Apply: Vintage Comic Books
source.text: Diamond wants to buy some vintage comic books from an online retailer. The price of a comic book is based on its condition, as shown. Diamond plans to buy some comic books that are in good and near mint condition and protective covers for $0.50 for each comic book. The retailer charges $9.99 for shipping. How could Diamond use an algebraic expression to find and compare the costs of different amounts of good and near mint condition comic books? Which combination of comic books would you recommend Diamond buy? three near mint and two good comic books two near mint and six good comic books one n

source.title: Apply: Football Plays
source.text: To make a first down, a football team must make at least a 10-yard gain from where they originally started, called the line of scrimmage. During a series of plays, a football team had a 10-yard loss, a 4-yard gain, a 3-yard loss, and a 21-yard gain.

source.title: Apply: Andrew’s Reasoning about Opposites
source.text: Choose a method. Solve independently, justify your answer, then check the goal.

source.title: Apply: Comparing Heights
source.text: Two of the tallest formations on Earth are Mount Everest and Mauna Kea. Mount Everest is a mountain in South Asia. Mauna Kea is a dormant volcano on the island of Hawaii.

source.title: Apply: A Game of Golf
source.text: Golf Scores are measured as over or under par. Par is the number of golf strokes considered necessary to get the golf ball in the hole. The winner is the player with the least score. The table shows the golf scores of six players after seven holes. They are playing a total of 9 holes.

source.title: Apply: Let’s Draw Shapes
source.text: What shape can you create on the coordinate plane that will have all of its vertices be reflections of each other? What are the coordinates of each vertex?

source.title: Apply: Deon’s Errands
source.text: What are the coordinates of the dry cleaner?

source.title: Apply: Maria’s Craft Store
source.text: Maria, a craft store owner, plans to rent a location in a shopping center and is considering the two spaces shown. Each unit represents one foot, so each line on the grid represents 5 feet. Space A has a monthly rental cost of $13.89 per square foot. Space B has a monthly rental cost of $13.49 per square foot. Maria wants to pay the lower total monthly rental price.

source.title: Apply: Blueberry Muffins
source.text: If Michael wants to have 24 blueberry muffins, which muffin mix and how many boxes of each mix would you recommend he purchase? Explain.

source.title: Apply: Margaret’s New Pet
source.text: Pugs weigh 32 pounds less than bulldogs. Irish Setters weigh 20 pounds more than bulldogs. Irish Terriers weigh 43 pounds less than Irish Setters. Shiba Inu weigh 5 pounds more than pugs.

source.title: Apply: Snack Bags
source.text: The student council buys snacks in bulk to sell during lunch. One box of snacks contains the types and quantities of snacks shown below. The first month, the student council sold 115 bags of snacks, including 50 bags of cheese crackers.

source.title: Apply: Festival Tickets
source.text: Four friends are doing yard work around town to earn money to attend the upcoming festival advertised in the flyer. They are charging $15 per hour for yard work. The four friends will combine their earnings.

source.title: Apply: Earning Money
source.text: Yuzuki wants to earn enough money to go on a class trip that costs $750. The image shows different ways she can earn money.

source.title: Apply: Selling Pizzas
source.text: At a local pizza shop, a customer can order up to three different toppings on a large pizza. The pizza shop has a total of 6 employees. The shop spends $1.15 on cheese and $1.95 on sauce for each pizza. How can you describe the relationship between the number of large pizzas sold and each of the following:

source.title: Apply: Nakai’s Savings Account
source.text: Nakai opened a savings account with an initial deposit, or principal, of $750. The account earns 3.5% simple interest each year. Interest is the amount paid or earned for the use of the principal. Interest is called simple interest when it is calculated using the principal amount. The graph shows the interest Nakai has earned over a period of time.

source.title: Apply: Music Downloads
source.text: Would you recommend that Diamond purchase or stream songs from the online music service?

source.title: Apply: Choosing Cupcakes
source.text: Yelina is comparing the costs of having cupcakes delivered from two different bakeries. Yelina has a budget of $110 to spend.
